steps.why: Python runs Meson; meson setup configures with the C compiler and meson compile builds with Ninja: the package installs the three.

steps.script: mkdir /tmp/amy-meson && cd /tmp/amy-meson && printf 'int main(void) { return 42; }\n' > main.c && printf '%s\n' "project('probe', 'c')" "executable('probe', 'main.c')" > meson.build && meson setup build && meson compile -C build; build/probe; test $? = 42 && man meson > /tmp/amy-man && grep -q build /tmp/amy-man && ! grep -Eq '^[.](TH|SH|Dd|Sh) ' /tmp/amy-man

steps.why: yes ends when its reader does.

steps.script: test "$(yes | head -n 3 | tr '\n' ' ')" = 'y y y ' && test "$(printf abc | sha1sum | cut -c 1-40)" = a9993e364706816aba3e25717850c26c9cd0d89d && printf abc | sha512sum | grep -q '^ddaf35a193617aba' && cal 10 2026 | grep -q 2026 && echo sponged > /tmp/amy-sponge && tr a-z A-Z < /tmp/amy-sponge | sponge /tmp/amy-sponge && grep -qx SPONGED /tmp/amy-sponge && uuencode /tmp/amy-sponge sponge | uudecode -o /tmp/amy-uu && cmp /tmp/amy-uu /tmp/amy-sponge

steps.why: A database written and queried; a second process is told that the first has it. The library links a program.

steps.script: sqlite3 /tmp/amy.db "create table word(n, name); insert into word values (6, 'six'), (7, 'seven'), (9, 'nine'); pragma journal_mode = wal" > /dev/null && test "$(sqlite3 /tmp/amy.db "select sum(n) * 3 + 3, json_group_array(name) from word where name like 's%'")" = '42|["six","seven"]' && sqlite3 /tmp/amy.db 'select count(*) from word' ".shell sqlite3 /tmp/amy.db 'select count(*) from word' 2>&1" | grep -q 'database is locked' && printf '%s\n' '#include <sqlite3.h>' "int main(void) { return sqlite3_libversion_number() != SQLITE_VERSION_NUMBER; }" > /tmp/amy-sqlite3.c && cc -O0 /tmp/amy-sqlite3.c -lsqlite3 -o /tmp/amy-sqlite3 && /tmp/amy-sqlite3

steps.script: mkdir -p /tmp/amy-zip/in/deep /tmp/amy-zip/out && cd /tmp/amy-zip && seq 1 2000 > in/deep/numbers && zip -q -r in.zip in && zip -T in.zip > /dev/null && unzip -q in.zip -d out && cmp out/in/deep/numbers in/deep/numbers && test "$(stat -c %s in.zip)" -lt "$(stat -c %s in/deep/numbers)"

steps.why: A module written from text is valid, reads back and loses its names to wasm-strip; a program cc links here is a module with 64-bit memory.

steps.script: cd /tmp && echo '(module (func $answer (export "answer") (result i32) i32.const 42))' > amy.wat && wat2wasm --debug-names amy.wat -o amy.wasm && wasm-validate amy.wasm && wasm2wat amy.wasm | grep -q 'i32.const 42' && wasm-objdump -x amy.wasm | grep -q answer && cp amy.wasm amy-named.wasm && wasm-strip amy.wasm && test "$(stat -c %s amy.wasm)" -lt "$(stat -c %s amy-named.wasm)" && echo 'int main(void) { return 0; }' > amy-wabt.c && cc amy-wabt.c -o amy-wabt && wasm-objdump -x amy-wabt | grep -q i64

steps.why: A grammar becomes a parser that counts its tokens, and a scanner counts the numbers it reads. flex comes with yacc.

steps.script: cd /tmp && printf '%s\n' '%{' 'int count; int yylex(void); void yyerror(const char *message) {}' '%}' '%token A' '%%' 'list: | list A { count++; };' '%%' '#include <stdio.h>' 'int yylex(void) { return getchar() == EOF ? 0 : A; }' 'int main(void) { yyparse(); return count; }' > amy.y && yacc -o amy-y.c amy.y && cc amy-y.c -o amy-y; printf abcdef | ./amy-y; test $? = 6

cd /tmp && printf '%s\n' '%{' 'static int numbers;' '%}' '%%' '[0-9]+ numbers++;' '.|\n ;' '%%' 'int main(void) { yylex(); return numbers; }' > amy.l && flex -o amy-l.c amy.l && cc amy-l.c -lfl -o amy-l; echo 'a 1 bb 22 c 333' | ./amy-l; test $? = 3 && lex --version > /dev/null

steps.why: The core's tar only unpacks files and directories. The tar package puts sbase's in its place: a tree with a link archived, listed and unpacked.
steps.script: mkdir -p /tmp/amy-tar/in/deep /tmp/amy-tar/out && cd /tmp/amy-tar && seq 1 2000 > in/deep/numbers && ln -s deep/numbers in/link && ! tar -cf in.tar in 2> /dev/null

steps.why: -z, -j and -J start gzip, bzip2 and xz, which the package installs, and wait for them: each archive is whole when tar ends.

steps.script: cd /tmp/amy-tar && tar -cf in.tar in && tar -xf in.tar -C out && cmp out/in/deep/numbers in/deep/numbers && test "$(readlink out/in/link)" = deep/numbers && tar -czf in.tgz in && tar -tzf in.tgz | grep -qx in/link && tar -cjf in.tbz in && tar -tjf in.tbz | grep -qx in/link && tar -cJf in.txz in && tar -tJf in.txz | grep -qx in/link
